citations.assessment: The fuller Hanan entry explicitly makes this proposal. The Bavli has the local patronymic and places Hanan in Rav’s company, without identifying the father beyond the name.

The Yalkut and Rabbeinu Gershom give Hanan bar Rava as Rav’s son-in-law. The Bavli prints a shorter identification in that narrative. The Shabbat exchange attests his participation in a teaching before Rav, while the formal pupil label remains the local author’s characterization.
The local Rabbah entry explicitly proposes the relation of the Hanan and Rava notices. The checked Bavli separately uses the name Rabbah bar Rav Hanan. Maintain the uncertainty.

holds.reason: The identification and implied genealogical alignment remain editorial proposals. Preserve the tentative wording.
